text:
jessica_pm: Heads-up: ACME wants "per-customer route isolation" so their ad-serving route doesn't compete with others. They want a 30-day pilot, predictable billing, and two "launch exemptions" per quarter. Thoughts?

raj_sales: they will pay for isolation but insist on simple on/off SLA and predictable cost. They said they can't accept multi-week provisioning.

nora_eng: tech constraints: isolation options: 1) logical QoS on shared pools (fast), 2) pinned dedicated pools (costly, slower to provision). pinned pools give stricter isolation and KV cache warmups, but increases infra ops.

jessica_pm: launch checklist proposal: pilot agreement, telemetry dashboard for per-route p95/p99, billing acceptance, and legal carveouts for exemptions. Must define what "exemption" means operationally.

ops_bot: provisioning ETA: automated dedicated pool spinup currently ~72 hours once API enabled. Manual fallback for emergency is longer. If we want <48h guarantee, need ~2 sprints of automation.

raj_sales: customer needs <72h. Can we promise 72h in pilot and commit to shorter timelines later?

legal: carveouts: recommend capping exemptions to two events per quarter, 72h each. Add notification window 72h prior and an emergency clause with higher overage rates if fail to notify. Also call out force-majeure.

nora_eng: runtime detail: if we route to dedicated pool we must pre-warm KV cache for current model/version. For short spikes, logical QoS with burst tokens may suffice and avoids warmup penalty. Need expected qps pattern from customer.

jessica_pm: ask ACME for 7-day traffic trace and expected launch dates. Also propose two pricing approaches to show them.

```json
{
  "optionA": "Reserve capacity addon - $9k/mo for up to 600k tokens + $0.014/extra token",
  "optionB": "Per-route slab - $10k/mo for up to 5 routes, $16k/mo for up to 15 routes",
  "surge_pricing": "emergency surcharge 2x base rate for sustained >72h without notice"
}
```

tom_finance: notes: option A = predictable revenue, easier to forecast unit economics. Option B maps to customer scale but more complex billing. Recommend A for pilot.

raj_sales: pilot ask: show them A with a 30-day trial at 50% discount to prove value. Then negotiate full price if SLOs met.

legal: include statement: "Provider reserves right to throttle after 72 hours of sustained surge; customer may request paid temporary dedicated pool with 48h notice when available."

nora_eng: infra estimate for short-term pilot (logical QoS + telemetry): ~1 dev-week + 0.5 SRE-week. For dedicated pool onboarding automation: ~2 dev-sprints.

jessica_pm: decision: run pilot as Reserve Capacity addon (option A) with logical QoS initially. If we see sustained launches that need pinned pools, convert to dedicated offering. Action items:
- jessica_pm: send ACME onboarding request and data ask by EOD today
- tom_finance: price sheet + 50% trial template by tomorrow morning
- legal: draft pilot clause + surge exemption language by EOD tomorrow
- nora_eng: quick infra checklist + rough effort estimate for both QC and dedicated pools by Monday
- raj_sales: confirm ACME accepts the 72h provisioning expectation for pilot

raj_sales: pinging ACME now. will report back. :rocket:
